findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the LLM-emitted severity surface (common.schema.json finding.severity `required`+enum, and the reviewer prompts ticket_quality/security/spec_alignment/code_quality/completion_verifier that instruct the model to emit `severity`) and specify per-child how each prompt and the schema enum/required-list are migrated when the field is dropped.
evidence: `common.schema.json#/$defs/finding` (L145) lists `severity` as `required` with enum {critical,high,medium,low,info} (L122-126) — an LLM structured-output contract

Reviewer prompts instruct the model to EMIT severity: `reviewers/ticket_quality.md:39` ("**severity**: one of critical, high, medium, low, info"), `reviewers/security.md:31`, `reviewers/spec_alignment.md:42`, `reviewers/code_quality.md:35`, `reviewers/completion_verifier.md:211`

The plan's "Why this is NOT a one-liner" traces only the kernel `severity_label` and three deterministic consumers (aggregate.py, adapter.py, workflow/steps.py); it does not name the model-emitted severity path or commit to editing those prompts / the schema enum+required list
findings.finding: The plan removes the `severity` field/enum from the finding shape but omits the LLM-EMITTED severity contract: several reviewer prompts instruct the model to emit `severity` as a required structured-output field, and the plan never specifies updating those prompts or the schema.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria ("No finding produced anywhere ... carries a `severity` key") and child `byzantine-spinelike-penguin`
scenarios: An executor of the final child removes `severity` from the schema/finding shape but leaves ticket_quality.md/security.md/spec_alignment.md still directing the model to emit it, producing schema-invalid model output or an orphaned field
The 5-level LLM enum vocabulary is silently retired with no replacement instruction to the reviewers
findings.suggested_fix: In child byzantine-spinelike-penguin (and its predecessors), add explicit steps to (a) drop `severity` from `common.schema.json#/$defs/finding` required+properties and delete the 5-level `severity` `$def`, and (b) edit every reviewer prompt that currently instructs the model to emit `severity` (ticket_quality.md, security.md, spec_alignment.md, code_quality.md, completion_verifier.md) to stop emitting it.

findings.checklist_item: State how existing on-disk verdict records are handled across the severity→priority cutover: bump `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (or make the reader tolerate/ignore old-shape entries by falling back to re-verification), confirm previously-signed completion certs remain readable (readers ignore the vestigial `severity` / do not require `priority`/`decision` on historical records), and note the back-out path for the persisted shape.
evidence: `common.schema.json` declares the finding shape with `"required": ["severity", "dimension", "detail"]` and `severity` `$ref`d there

completion_verdict findings use `"items": { "$ref": "common.schema.json#/$defs/finding" }`, so removing `severity` (and requiring `priority`/`decision`) changes the read/validate path for every persisted verdict

`completion_verdict_cache.py` persists validated verdicts to disk keyed by criterion hash with `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`; the plan does not mention bumping the version or invalidating/migrating old-shape entries
`transition_close.sign_completion_verdict` signs verdicts as certs; old certs embed the old finding shape (with `severity`, no `priority`/`decision`) and are immutable once signed
ABSENCE: the plan's BREAKING note covers CHANGELOG/release-notes (breakage acknowledgement) but says nothing about reading back or back-out for records already on disk
findings.finding: Child #6 removes the `severity` field (a REQUIRED property of the `finding` shape in common.schema.json) and adds `priority`/`decision`, but the plan never states how EXISTING persisted verdict records written under the old shape are handled after the cutover — specifically the cross-run PASS cache (`.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json`, which carries `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`) and previously-SIGNED completion-verdict certs whose embedded findings carry `severity` and lack `priority`/`decision`.
findings.location: Decomposition child 6 (byzantine-spinelike-penguin: 'drop the severity field from the finding shape (BREAKING)'); Acceptance Criteria 'No finding … carries a severity key'
scenarios: After the field-drop lands, a re-verify reads a stale cached verdict written under the old shape; if the reader/validator now expects `priority`/`decision` (or rejects the absent-`severity` case differently), the cached PASS may be silently discarded, mis-interpreted, or raise
A previously-signed completion cert is re-read by a consumer that now assumes the new finding shape, so historical attestations no longer validate against the current schema
findings.suggested_fix: In child #6, add a compatibility note: keep the finding-schema readers backward-tolerant (do not make `priority`/`decision` a hard `required` for records read from disk, and ignore residual `severity`), bump the completion-verdict cache schema version so pre-cutover entries are naturally invalidated and safely re-verified (fail-open), and document that signed historical certs are read leniently so the change is reversible without corrupting persisted state.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` (`_to_common_finding`, shim.py:66, and its `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` at 33-38) to the affected-site inventory and assign it to a child (child 4/6), and re-derive the full consumer list via `find_referencing_symbols` on `severity_label`/`_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` plus a string grep for `"severity"` across all of `src/rebar/`, not just the two named dirs.

adapter.py:85-86 comment: 'mirrors the WS4 shim' — the shim is the code-review sibling of the named adapter.py consumer
findings.finding: The severity-retirement inventory omits src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py's `_to_common_finding`, a concrete consumer that owns its own `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` map (shim.py:33-38) and writes a finding-shape `"severity"` key (shim.py:66) into every code-review `review_result`. The plan's traced list and child decomposition name review_bot/adapter.py (child 4), aggregate.py (child 3), and workflow/steps.py (child 5) but never the shim — even though adapter.py's own comment says its map 'mirrors the WS4 shim'.
findings.location: 'Why this is NOT a one-liner (traced)' consumer list and Decomposition children 3-6; AC #2 grep scope `src/rebar/llm/`
scenarios: No child ticket patches shim.py:66, so after the field drop the code-review `review_result` findings still carry `severity`, and AC #2's `grep ... src/rebar/llm/` still matches shim.py:66 — the epic cannot close on its own criterion.

If shim.py:33-38's `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` is left after decide.py stops emitting the kernel severity label, `_to_common_finding` silently defaults every code-review finding to `_SEVERITY_DEFAULT` ('medium'), corrupting the aggregate.py ranking that child 3 is trying to fix.

The code-review review_result surface (the WS4 `review_code` path) is not assigned to any child, so it under-delivers the blocking/advisory migration relative to the Gerrit and CLI surfaces child 4 covers.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend child 4 (or child 6) to cover the code-review shim: replace shim.py's severity stamping in `_to_common_finding` with the blocking/advisory + priority shape and delete shim.py's local `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`, mirroring the adapter.py change; note it in the traced consumer list alongside adapter.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the fail_on_severity migration (and DET-priority child), state the concrete priority threshold and the old-severity->priority mapping, and add a check that existing gate outcomes are preserved (or document the intended behavior change).
evidence: Plan: 'A high-impact/low-validity finding shows as critical while ranking below a major' — establishes the two signals order differently.
Plan: 'migrate the fail_on_severity workflow gate to a priority threshold' names no concrete threshold value or old->new mapping.
Plan: 'assign fixed priority to DET-tier findings' names no priority values.
findings.finding: The migration of `fail_on_severity` to a priority threshold (child camlet-exodermal-kodiakbear) and the fixed priorities assigned to DET-tier findings (child uncheering-uncivil-pig) introduce numeric cutoffs/values that are asserted at the parent level without a stated mapping from the old severity levels to a concrete priority threshold. Because priority = validity x impact orders differently than the old impact-only severity, a naive cutoff can silently change which findings gate a build (a previously-blocking `major` may fall below the cutoff, or a high-impact/low-validity finding that was `critical` may now block).
findings.location: Decomposition items 2 and 5; 'migrate the fail_on_severity workflow gate to a priority threshold'
findings.suggested_fix: In camlet-exodermal-kodiakbear, pin the default priority cutoff and show how each legacy fail_on_severity level (critical/high/...) maps to it; add a fixture asserting a representative old-gating finding produces the same block/advisory outcome under the new threshold.
